My dad just called to tell me my cousin got placed at a firm with a 35 LPA package, and then he casually asked about my preparation for the upcoming midterms. He didn't say it directly, but I know he's thinking my 7.2 CGPA is a waste of his money and I'll end up unemployed. I feel this massive, suffocating pressure in my chest that I'm just a disappointment who will never make them proud.

The professor praised my lab report in front of the whole class today, and instead of feeling good, I literally went to the washroom to throw up. Now I'm staring at the next assignment completely paralyzed because the bar is set so high, and I know my next submission is going to reveal how stupid I actually am. The praise feels like a death sentence.

I somehow cleared the Amazon winter internship drive, but I feel like an absolute fraud. The interviewer literally asked me the easiest binary tree question from Leetcode while my roommate, who is easily ten times better at DSA than me, got grilled on hard DP problems and ended up getting rejected. Everyone in our batch is congratulating me and asking me for preparation tips on LinkedIn, but I’m literally sweating bullets thinking about day one when they realize I can't write a clean production-grade API to save my life. I just got incredibly lucky, and the guilt of taking a spot that belonged to someone actually smart is eating me alive.

My parents just posted my 9.4 CGPA marksheet on our extended family WhatsApp group, and everyone is calling me a genius, but I feel like throwing up. Honestly, the only reason my grades are this high is because the professors recycled previous years' papers and the grading rubrics were super lenient this semester. I have a physical viva exam coming up next Tuesday, and I’m terrified that the moment the external examiner asks me a conceptual question, I’m going to freeze and show everyone that I’m actually just a mediocre crammer who doesn't understand real engineering.

I got selected as the team lead for our college's Smart India Hackathon team, and instead of being happy, I've spent the last three days paralyzingly anxious. The other four guys on the team are brilliant—one of them literally built an open-source library and another is a competitive programmer—and here I am, just a decent manager who can make nice slides. I keep thinking they’ll look at me during the coding phase and realize I have absolutely no technical authority to guide them, and we’ll fail because of my incompetence.

Professor Mehta wrote 'Excellent depth of analysis' on my research proposal draft and shared it with the entire class as an exemplar. I should be on cloud nine, but I feel physically sick; it feels like I've accidentally set a bar so high that there is absolutely no way I can maintain it for the actual paper. I spent weeks staring at a blank Google Doc now because every sentence I write feels incredibly stupid compared to that draft, and I'm convinced he's going to read my final submission and realize the draft was just a fluke.

I got placed at a firm with a 12 LPA package, which is honestly more than I ever dreamed of. But at dinner tonight, my dad was talking to my uncle and kept downplaying it, saying 'Oh, it’s just a non-core support role, not like Sharma ji's son who got 24 LPA SDE-1 at Directi.' It instantly triggered this voice in my head that says my placement was a fluke, that I only got in because of the diversity hiring quota, and that I'm going to get fired within the probation period because I don't belong there. I feel so small and useless even after working my ass off for three years.

I somehow cleared the day-1 shortlist for the high-frequency trading firm, and my CGPA is a 9.4, but I feel like throwing up. I literally just memorized the exact patterns for those DSA graphs last week, and the interviewer happened to ask the exact same questions. When they put me on a live coding screen tomorrow, they’re going to realize I can’t even write a basic BFS without stuttering. I'm a fraud who got lucky, and the drop from here is going to destroy me.

Everyone is spamming congratulations on our batch WhatsApp group because I got the FAANG internship, but my chest is so tight I can barely breathe. I only got in because the interviewer was incredibly nice and basically guided me to the solution when I froze up on the dynamic programming question. I didn't 'earn' this, I just manipulated a kind stranger into hiring a dummy, and now I have to go there and fail publicly.

My professor wrote 'Outstanding work, very intuitive approach' on my compiler design project, and I felt instantly sick to my stomach. He has no idea I spent 40 hours crying over stack overflow and basically copy-pasted the structure from an old GitHub repo. I feel like a thief who stole a grade from the actually brilliant kids in the front row who understand the actual theory.

The seniors made me the lead for our Smart India Hackathon team because they think I'm some coding prodigy just because I have a decent CGPA. I am literally dying inside because I don't even know how to set up a Docker container without looking up a tutorial every single time. They are counting on me to architect the whole system, and I’m just waiting for the moment they realize I'm a complete clown who knows nothing.

I just got awarded the merit scholarship for our department, which covers half my tuition, and instead of being happy, I’m sitting on my hostel bed sobbing. I keep checking the PDF to see if there's a typo in the roll number and they meant to email someone else. My roommate, who actually understands system design instead of just memorizing slides like me, got nothing, and I feel like an absolute criminal.

I just got my midterms back and somehow scored a 9.4 CGPA. Instead of feeling happy, my stomach completely dropped. I'm literally shaking because I know it was just a fluke, and now everyone—my professor, my batchmates—is going to expect me to keep this up, and they'll eventually find out I actually have no idea what I'm doing in the DSA lab.

My entire WhatsApp group is flooded with screenshots of summer internship offer letters, and my feed is just endless 'I am thrilled to announce' posts. I got a decent offer too, but I can't shake the feeling that the HR made a mistake or they only hired me to fill some diversity quota. I'm terrified that when the day-one onboarding starts, they'll realize I can barely write a clean Python script without looking up documentation.

Our system design professor praised my project during the viva today in front of the whole class. He literally said my architecture was elegant. I wanted to crawl under my desk and die because my partner did the database schema and I just put the presentation together and wrote some basic API endpoints. I feel like an absolute thief who stole someone else's credit, and I'm dreading the final coding run next week because I'll definitely mess it up.

I cleared the first two rounds of the on-campus placements, but I honestly feel like I just got lucky with easy questions. I keep seeing my peers who are 10x better coders than me getting rejected, which makes me feel like an absolute fraud. How can I walk into the final HR round tomorrow when I know I'm sitting in a spot that one of my brilliant classmates actually deserves?

My dad called today because he heard our neighbor's kid got a 45 LPA package. He didn't outright yell, but he said 'We have high hopes for you, you've always been our star child.' My chest feels so tight. I've been struggling so hard in my DBMS classes and my last mock test score was terrible, but they still think I'm some genius who will easily land a massive package. If they knew how much I'm drowning, they would be so disgusted.

I just got a summer internship at a tier-1 firm, but I feel like throwing up. In the final round, the interviewer literally asked me the exact same dynamic programming question I ran on LeetCode the night before, so I just coded it from memory. Everyone on our class WhatsApp group is congratulating me and calling me a DSA god, but I’m terrified they'll find out I actually suck and just got incredibly lucky.

They just put up the midterms merit list and I somehow got a 9.4 CGPA. Instead of feeling happy, my stomach is in knots because I know the next set of papers are going to be way harder. I keep thinking, 'This is it, this is the semester where I drop to a 7 and everyone realizes I’ve been winging it this whole time.'

We had a mock group discussion today for campus placements, and everyone was talking so fluently about system design and microservices. I just sat there nodding like an idiot, praying the coordinator wouldn't point at me. I cleared my coding rounds last week, but hearing them make so much sense makes me feel like my passing score was just a glitch in the system.

My dad just called to ask if I've started preparing for the Amazon coding test, saying our neighbor's son got a 40 LPA package there. I couldn't even explain to him that my basic pointer concepts are still shaky and I struggle to write simple recursive trees without looking at solutions. I feel like a massive disappointment waiting to happen, pretending to be this smart engineering kid when I'm actually empty inside.
